fractals.name: Fractals: Infinite Within Finite
fractals.truth: Infinite complexity from finite rules. Dimensions between integers. D = log(N)/log(S). Self-similarity across scales.
fractals.qfep_connection: Fractals embody the QFEP tension directly: F (deterministic recursive rule) + λE(S) (random variation in stochastic fractals) creates forms at the edge of chaos. The Mandelbrot boundary is where order meets chaos—infinitely complex yet bounded. Fractals are queer geometry: dimensionally non-normative, nowhere smooth, computationally irreducible.
fractals.demonstration: Walk inside the Menger sponge. Watch the stochastic tree grow with random variation. Zoom into the Mandelbrot boundary and see infinite detail.
fractals.description: Self-similarity across scales, infinite complexity from finite rules. Fractals refuse integer dimensions—they exist between 1D and 2D, between line and plane. The Mandelbrot boundary is infinitely complex yet bounded; the Sierpinski triangle has zero area yet infinite structure. This is queer geometry: dimensionally non-normative, nowhere smooth, computationally irreducible.
learning_objectives: Self-similarity: the whole contains copies of itself
Fractal dimension: D = log(N)/log(S) — between integers
Recursion as emergence: simple rules, infinite complexity
Edge of chaos: Mandelbrot boundary, Julia variations
